title: Iterating a Linear Function with Itself
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let $f(x)=2x-3$. Compute the self-composite $(f\circ f)(x)$ and simplify it to the form $ax+b$.

steps.title: Write the Self-Composition
steps.explanation: Apply the rule $f(u)=2u-3$ to the input $u=f(x)$.
steps.why: A function composed with itself still follows the inside-out evaluation order.

steps.title: Substitute the Inner Formula
steps.explanation: Replace $f(x)$ inside the outer copy with $2x-3$, keeping the parentheses.
steps.why: Parentheses prevent the factor of $2$ from being distributed incorrectly.

steps.title: Expand and Combine Constants
steps.explanation: Distributing gives $4x-6$, and subtracting the final $3$ yields $4x-9$.
steps.why: Collecting like terms puts the composite back in linear form.
